item.content:encoded:
By KEN POWTAK
Updated 10:25 PM EDT, September 23, 2026
BOSTON (AP) — Sonny Gray pitched six innings to tie Philadelphia’s Cristopher Sánchez for the major league lead with his 18th victory, Andruw Monasterio drove in the only run with a sixth-inning single, and the Boston Red Sox edged Cleveland 1-0 on Wednesday night to snap the Guardians’ six-game winning streak.
It was just the fifth win in 13 games for the Red Sox, who clinched a playoff spot on Sunday.
The 36-year-old Gray (18-5) is in line to become the fourth Red Sox pitcher since 2000 to lead the AL in victories, joining Rick Porcello (2016), Josh Beckett (’07) and Curt Schilling (’04).
Gray allowed four singles, struck out three, walked one and lowered his ERA to 2.72.
Aroldis Chapman struck out the side in the ninth for his 35th save of the season.
Cleveland starter Foster Griffin (15-6) gave up a run on 10 hits with seven strikeouts.
The Guardians remained one game ahead of the Chicago White Sox atop the AL Central, after Chicago lost 5-4 to Kansas City on Wednesday night. The Guardians needed a win Wednesday combined with a loss by either Texas or Houston to clinch a postseason berth.
The victory came with a price for the Red Sox when center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela left with right hamstring tightness after running out a single the same day he was activated from the injured list. He had been sidelined with a right a quad strain since Sept. 3 and made a diving headlong grab on Steven Kwan, the game’s first batter.
Jarren Duran singled leading off the sixth, advanced on a groundout and barely beat left fielder Kwan’s throw with a headfirst slide on Monasterio’s hit.
Up next
Red Sox LHP Ranger Suarez (8-4, 3.27 ERA) is slated to start the series finale Thursday. The Guardians had not named a starter.

item.content:encoded:
Sonny Gray (18-5, 2.72 ERA) finished his marvelous regular season with another strong performance, firing six shutout innings on 77 pitches, allowing four hits and one walk while striking out three. Next start? Game 1 or 2 of next week’s AL Wild Card Series, all but certain to be at Yankee Stadium.
“He looked fantastic,” said Red Sox manager Chad Tracy. “Had his spin. Was in the zone. Was ahead in the count. He looked really good. It was good to see.”
Even better to see was the return of All-Star closer Aroldis Chapman, who hadn’t pitched since Sept. 13 because of a lat issue. All the 38-year-old did was overpower the Guardians by striking out the side (all swinging) in order on 12 pitches. That’s all it took for career save No. 402 and 35th this season.
“I felt good and happy to be able to go out there,” said Chapman. “I felt like my pitches and my stuff were very good today. So I’m happy to be back. I feel normal. I feel like I’m at 100 percent right now.”
That is certainly good news for the Red Sox, who need their closer in top form to make a deep postseason run.
“He looked sharp,” said Tracy. “That was also really good to see.”
For the first time in weeks, Tracy was able to deploy his 7-8-9 relief crew in Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Chapman. All three relievers had injuries at various times down the stretch but are trending well now.
“That was great,” said Tracy. “To be perfectly honest with you, that was kind of planned out regardless of how the game went. So to be able to score a run prior to that section of relievers coming in was fantastic.”
And while hits with runners in scoring position (2-for-14, 11 left on base) were again a rare commodity for Boston, Andruw Monasterio broke out of an 0-for-21 slump by belting an RBI single with two outs in the sixth that scored Jarren Duran from second.
In a game in which neither team had an extra-base hit, combining instead for 17 singles, Monasterio’s knock was the difference in the ballgame.
“I was fighting myself just yesterday and tonight about my approach,” said Monasterio. “I just had to get through it. And I did it.”
In this final homestand of the regular season, the main focus for the Red Sox is having their house in order for what’s to come next week.
There was some cause for concern in that regard, as center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela, after his first at-bat back from a three-week absence with a right quadriceps strain, had to exit in the top of the third with right hamstring tightness.
The Red Sox are hopeful it was a mild setback.
“I think it was just a cramp,” said Rafaela. “Maybe not hydrated enough. And I got that cramp right there and just didn't want to risk going for the double. And then, obviously, it’s Trace just trying to protect me, with big things in front of us. And so I think it's just that.”

item.title: [sentinelandenterprise.com] Sonny Gray’s scoreless start powers Red Sox to close win over Guardians

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox pulled off a 1-0 series-evening win over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night, despite the ongoing dearth of situational hitting that has plagued them for the last two weeks and intermittently throughout the season.
Boston batters tallied 12 hits, but went 2 for 14 with runners in scoring position, and left 11 men on base in eight innings.
Fortunately for the home team, Sonny Gray was on form in his final start of the regular season. The veteran right-hander tossed six shutout innings, with four hits, one walk and three strikeouts.
Gray’s sixth scoreless start of at least six innings this year tied his single-season high first set in 2015 and matched in 2025. He is the first Red Sox pitcher to make at least six such starts in his age-36 season or older since Luis Tiant in 1977, and only the fourth in franchise history (also Cy Young, Lefty Grove).
“Just a really good pitcher,” manager Chad Tracy said of his starter. “The level of consistency for him from start to finish has been very fun to watch, and impressive.”
Though Gray’s pitch count sat at 77 (52 for strikes) after the sixth and the game remained scoreless, Tracy went to his bullpen. With Boston’s postseason ticket punched on Sunday, the short hook could suggest Gray is getting the ball for Game 1 of the Wild Card series on Tuesday.
Cleveland southpaw Foster Griffin was not nearly as adept at keeping the Red Sox off the diamond. He struck out seven and issued no walks, but yielded 10 hits in six innings of one-run ball.
Save for Jarren Duran’s leadoff single and Andruw Monasterio’s two-out RBI single in the sixth, the Red Sox bailed Griffin out every time. They were 2 for 11 RISP through his six innings. Their nine men left on base during Griffin’s start included multiple in four of the first five frames and bases-loaded in the third.
“Yeah, I mean, take the positives,” Tracy said of the offense. “I thought we swung the bat great. We actually got some hits today. … Between (the two-out hits) and the accumulation of hits and base runners throughout the game, I thought it was a pretty good offensive night. Obviously you’d like to score more, but we did take better plate appearances.”
Tyron Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman, Boston’s elite bullpen trio all season long, ensured the slim lead held until the end with a scoreless inning apiece. Tracy revealed postgame their appearances were “planned out, regardless of how the game went.”
“That was great,” Tracy said. “To be able to score a run prior to that section of relievers coming in was fantastic.”
Duran, who replaced Ceddanne Rafaela in center field in the top of the third, led off the bottom of the eighth with a single. His subsequent steal of second made 2026 his second career season with 20 home runs and 20 stolen bases (also 2024). Duran, Mookie Betts and Jackie Jensen are the only players in franchise history with multiple 20-20 seasons.
Rafaela’s first game back from a 10-day stint on the injured list with a right quad strain began in energetic fashion. He recorded each of the first three outs, including a diving catch to rob Guardians hitter Steven Kwan of a leadoff single.
But after pulling up lame at first base on his own leadoff single in the bottom of the second, Rafaela ultimately left the game with right hamstring tightness when the inning turned over. Tracy announced postgame that Rafaela will undergo an MRI on Thursday.
“No, I think it’s more frustrating (than disappointing),” Tracy said of the Rafaela situation. “You want to see everybody get to that finish line healthy.
“So more just when you see it, you’re concerned, you know? So (we) don’t know where we’re at with it yet. Hopefully, it’s not a huge deal, but still, yeah, makes your heart jump a little bit, and we’ll see where he’s at.”
Cleveland threatened against Whitlock in an eighth inning that saw both teams run out of ABS challenges. No. 9 hitter Brayan Rocchio led off with a single, and Whitlock issued a one-out walk to third baseman José Ramírez before getting an inning-ending double play from designated hitter Chase DeLauter.
After the Red Sox stranded Duran in the bottom of the eighth, Chapman took the mound for the first time since Sept. 13. Boston’s All-Star closer was back in top form after being day-to-day with lat tightness. He struck out the side, Jo Adell, and pinch-hitters Angel Martínez and Angel Genao on 12 pitches.
The Red Sox are 85-73 with four games left to play. Wednesday marked Tracy’s first win since the interim tag was removed on Tuesday.

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Sonny Gray proves doubters wrong with strong first season starting for the Red Sox in big-market Boston - The Boston Globe
item.dc:creator: Alex Speier

item.content:encoded:
When the Red Sox landed Sonny Gray in a deal with the Cardinals last November, a question hovered: Could the righthander handle life in a fishbowl?
Gray’s first 13 big league seasons had spanned the country, starting on the West Coast (Athletics, 2013-17), crossing over to the East Coast (Yankees, 2017-18), then settling into the Midwest (Reds, 2019-21; Twins, 2022-23; Cardinals, 2024-25). Across teams, he’d mostly been good or great, achieving All-Star recognition in Oakland, Cincinnati, and Minnesota, while notching two 200-strikeout seasons in St. Louis.
There was only one place where he didn’t live up to expectations: New York. As a result, some in the baseball industry concluded Gray was best suited for smaller markets.
Gray, who had the right to veto a trade anywhere he didn’t want to pitch, was aware of the suggestion. Perhaps for that reason, he needed little prodding to approve the trade to the Sox in hopes of laying waste to the suggestion.
“People doubted me just because of my size [entering pro ball]. Stupid, right? So maybe that is something that motivates me: people that talk [expletive] for no reason, just proving them wrong,” said Gray. “Maybe [proving people wrong] does have a little bit of extra motivation inside of me.
“When I left New York in 2018, I told myself that I’m going to go back to a big market at some point in my career. Especially after learning what I learned and having the experiences that I had [in New York], I knew I could [succeed] anywhere after that. So I always told myself that I was going to [pitch again in a large market].”
In the Sox’ 1-0 win Wednesday night over the Guardians, Gray concluded a regular season that served as a compelling testament to his ability to excel in one of the most-scrutinized baseball environments.
With six shutout innings, he finished the year at 18-5 with a 2.72 ERA, setting new career bests in wins and ERA while excelling as a low-velocity, pitch-to-contact artist. He allowed one or no runs in 14 starts.
On and off the mound, the 36-year-old found comfort in Boston, performing at an elite level and comfortable with the intimacy of Fenway and the area.
“I’ve really enjoyed the city. I’ll call it more of like a town, because that’s more what it feels like to me,” said Gray. “[But] I would say this is a pretty big [market]. I’ve enjoyed it. You never know what to expect, but I think the people have been great. I think Fenway is awesome. It’s a very special place.”
Through his comfort, Gray’s success seemingly answered any lingering questions about whether his comfort was tethered to his environment.
“His time in New York was tough and he knows that. I’m sure he wanted to go back and be like, ‘It wasn’t about the market,’ ” said Guardians manager Steven Vogt, who as a former Athletics teammate was behind the plate for the most games and innings thrown by Gray of any catcher in the pitcher’s career, and still considers him a close friend. “Every athlete’s wired differently. But I think for Sonny, getting another opportunity to pitch in a market like this, I think was important to him, and I’m glad that he got to do it.”
Now, Gray will have the opportunity to prove himself as a Red Sox in a different context: the postseason. History suggests he doesn’t fear the stage.
In 2013, as a 23-year-old rookie with just 10 big league starts on his résumé, Gray got the Game 2 starting assignment from the Athletics in the AL Division Series against Tigers ace of aces Justin Verlander, who at that point had six All-Star appearances along with Rookie of the Year, Cy Young, and MVP hardware.
Gray didn’t blink, engaging in an epic pitcher’s duel. Verlander logged seven shutout innings, while Gray posted eight zeros — both pitchers receiving no-decisions in an eventual 1-0 Athletics walkoff win.
“That was one of the greatest games I’ve ever been a part of,” said a beaming Vogt. “You’ve got Justin Verlander, who’d already cemented his path to Cooperstown. Sonny Gray’s throwing his first postseason game in his first season, and going into it, his demeanor, he just was not worried. He was not. He just wanted to go out and pitch.
“That’s the thing about Sonny. He’s one of the fiercest competitors I’ve ever been around. He’s calm, cool, and collected when he’s on the mound, but he’s a killer when he’s on the mound. … They just kept throwing knockouts back and forth.
“It’s his preparation. It’s who he is. He’s always been confident. He’s always been quiet. He’s always just kind of been ready for the moment. There’s no moment too big for him because he’s ready for anything. So I don’t think any of us were shocked that night. It was just more of, we got to watch that.”
Across six career postseason starts, the most recent coming in 2023 with the Twins, Gray is 1-3 with a 3.26 ERA. His teams have won three of his six outings. He is lined up to start for the Sox in next week’s Wild Card Series, likely in New York against the Yankees — affording him one more opportunity to dispel a narrative about his career.
How might that play out?
“If he was on my team,” said Vogt, “there’s no one else I’d rather pitch in a big game.”
Alex Speier can be reached at alex.speier@globe.com. Follow him @alexspeier.

item.content:encoded:
Sonny Gray, Red Sox shut out Guardians, who remain 1 up on White Sox
(Photo credit: Gregory Fisher)
Andruw Monasterio's sixth-inning RBI single and Sonny Gray's six shutout innings propelled the Boston Red Sox to a 1-0 win over the visiting Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night.
The Red Sox (85-73) managed the lone run on 12 hits, all singles. They went 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position and left eight men on base through five innings before Monasterio's run-scoring, two-out knock off Cleveland starter Foster Griffin (15-6) broke the deadlock.
In the sixth, Jarren Duran (2-for-3) lined a leadoff single to left and moved to second on a groundout. He scored from second base on Monasterio's knock, sliding ahead of left fielder Steven Kwan's relay throw and catcher Patrick Bailey's tag.
Gray (18-5) struck out three while allowing four hits and one walk to increase his American League-leading win total. Tyron Guerrero, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman each threw a scoreless inning to finish off Boston's 17th shutout victory of the season.
Chapman struck out the side in the ninth to log his 35th save as Boston snapped a three-game losing streak.
Red Sox center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela returned from a 17-game injury absence caused by a right quad strain to record all three outs in the first, including a spectacular diving catch on Kwan, the leadoff hitter who still went 2-for-4 for Cleveland (82-76).
Griffin worked six frames, striking out seven and allowing one run on 10 hits and no walks.
The Guardians remained one game up on the White Sox (81-77) in the American League Central after Chicago lost 5-4 at Kansas City on Wednesday.
Rafaela hit a leadoff single in the second inning but appeared to be in pain after reaching first. He stayed in the game to run the bases and initially took his defensive position before Duran replaced him. The Red Sox announced that Rafaela was dealing with right hamstring tightness.
Rafaela's defense helped Gray retire the first six men he faced. Bailey recorded Cleveland's first hit with a leadoff single in the third, but a 6-3 double play ended the inning without any damage. Gray fanned a pair of Guardians to strand two to end the fourth.
After the lone run scored and Gray exited, Guerrero struck out three in the seventh after a leadoff walk. Whitlock worked around Brayan Rocchio's leadoff single and Jose Ramirez's one-out walk in the eighth, inducing an inning-ending double-play grounder from Chase DeLauter.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox have secured a postseason berth. Now they need their offense to look ready for October. Boston enters Wednesday’s game against the Cleveland Guardians on a three-game losing streak. The Red Sox have scored two runs or fewer in each of those losses, putting more attention on the lineup Chad Tracy will send out against Cleveland left-hander Foster Griffin.
Jahmai Jones is batting third again, between Nick Sogard and Wilyer Abreu. Roman Anthony leads off, while Adley Rutschman bats fifth after collecting three hits, including two doubles, in Tuesday’s 3-2 loss.
The Red Sox announced Wednesday’s lineup ahead of the 7:10 p.m. ET game at Fenway Park.
Red Sox Lineup Vs. Guardians On Wednesday
- Roman Anthony, LF
- Nick Sogard, 1B
- Jahmai Jones, DH
- Wilyer Abreu, RF
- Adley Rutschman, C
- Ceddanne Rafaela, CF
- Caleb Durbin, 3B
- Trevor Story, SS
- Andruw Monasterio, 2B
Sonny Gray will start for Boston against Griffin.
Tonight's crew. pic.twitter.com/80BRyMRZI7
— Red Sox (@RedSox) September 23, 2026
Jones’ place in the order is worth watching. Batting him third puts a right-handed hitter between Sogard and Abreu against a left-handed starter. It also gives Jones another opportunity to strengthen his case for a significant postseason role.
Offense Needs To Step Up
Rutschman gave Boston one of its few bright spots Tuesday, but the Red Sox could not build enough offense around him. Mickey Gasper’s pinch-hit homer tied the game in the eighth inning before Cleveland pulled out the win. Boston has dropped five of its last seven games.
Gray enters Wednesday with a 17-5 record and a 2.82 ERA. A strong outing from him would help stop the skid, but the Red Sox also need to see more from a lineup that has gone quiet at an uncomfortable time.
Boston is postseason-bound. Wednesday offers a chance to start playing like it.

item.title: [foxnews.com] Sonny Gray and the Boston Red Sox host Cleveland Guardians in a potential MLB playoffs preview
item.dc:creator: David Troy
item.description: The end of the MLB Season is almost here, with roughly five games remaining, including today, for most teams. There are still some exciting matchups today and this weekend. We went just 1-1 yesterday, with a loss on the Angels and a win in the Rays-Yankees game. I suppose I should know better than to back a 100-loss team. Tonight, I'm going for a game that we could potentially see in the playoffs as the Guardians take on the Red Sox. The Guardians are currently the owners of the top spot in the
item.content:encoded:
The end of the MLB Season is almost here, with roughly five games remaining, including today, for most teams. There are still some exciting matchups today and this weekend. We went just 1-1 yesterday, with a loss on the Angels and a win in the Rays-Yankees game. I suppose I should know better than to back a 100-loss team.
Tonight, I'm going for a game that we could potentially see in the playoffs as the Guardians take on the Red Sox.
The Guardians are currently the owners of the top spot in the American League Central. As seems to be the case for Cleveland every season, they saved their best baseball for the end of the season. They've won six straight games, but they are only one game ahead of the White Sox, who have also won three straight games. The good news for both of them is that, as long as they both are winning games, they can both make the postseason. The magic number for the Guardians to make the playoffs is down to one.
This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.
Giving them a great chance today is the arm they acquired at the trade deadline, Foster Griffin. For the season, Griffin is 15-5 with a 3.67 ERA and a 1.19 WHIP. Griffin, overall, has been a nice addition to the team. He has two starts that were a little bit of a disaster, going four innings against the Mets and allowing five earned in his debut with the Guardians.
The Baltimore Orioles also knocked him around for eight runs in 2.1 innings. His other six starts saw him going for 22 innings and allow just 11 runs. He has never faced the Red Sox, so he could have them off balance the first time through the lineup.
The Boston Red Sox are one of those teams that are likely brimming with confidence. After a disaster of a start to their season, they pivoted and became one of the hottest teams in baseball right before the All-Star Break. They continue to be a streaky team, but the majority of their streaks have seen them winning games instead of losing them. They are still just an average team at Fenway with a 38-38 record for the season. It is almost hard to believe given how good they've been, but getting to .500 is impressive because of how bad they were early in the year.
The Red Sox are sending the one guy who was dominant at home all year, Sonny Gray. For the season, Sonny Gray is 17-5 with a 2.82 ERA and a 1.16 WHIP. He should be in the running for the Cy Young Award, even though he won't win over Cam Schlittler. He's been solid in September, going 19.1 innings and allowing a total of six earned runs. He faced the Guardians earlier this season and allowed just one earned run over six innings in a 9-1 win for the Red Sox.
It wasn't just that one game against the Guardians that Gray has excelled in. He has been great against them for years, holding hitters to a .208 batting average over 130 at-bats. Although the Red Sox don't really "need" this game to solidify their Wild Card spot, they still should look to win. Gray has been dominant for them, and they've been very successful in his outings this year. I'm backing the Red Sox here and I also think they probably cover the -1.5 run line. I also would be surprised to see this game go under 6.5 runs. I'll play all three bets.
For more sports betting information and plays, follow David on X/Twitter: @futureprez2024

item.content:encoded:
El final de la temporada de la Liga Americana ( MLB ) está a la vuelta de la esquina, y a la mayoría de los equipos les quedan unas cinco jornadas, contando la de hoy. Todavía hay algunos partidos emocionantes hoy y este fin de semana. Ayer nos fue 1-1: perdimos con los Angels y ganamos en el partido entre los Rays y los Yankees. Supongo que debería saber que no hay que apostar por un equipo que lleva 100 derrotas.
Esta noche voy a ver un partido que quizá podamos volver a ver en los playoffs: los Guardians se enfrentan a los Red Sox.
Los Guardians ocupan ahora mismo el primer puesto de la División Central de la Liga Americana. Como suele pasar con Cleveland cada temporada, han reservado su mejor juego para el final de la temporada. Han ganado seis partidos seguidos, pero solo llevan un partido de ventaja sobre los White Sox, que también llevan tres victorias seguidas. La buena noticia para ambos es que, mientras sigan ganando partidos, los dos pueden clasificarse para la postemporada. El número mágico para que los Guardians se clasifiquen para los playoffs se ha reducido a uno.
Esta página puede contener enlaces de afiliados a socios de apuestas deportivas legales. Si te registras o realizas una apuesta, FOX News podría recibir una compensación. Este contenido lo ha creado un equipo que trabaja de forma independiente de la redacción de FOX News.
Hoy tienen una gran oportunidad gracias al lanzador que ficharon en el cierre del mercado de traspasos: Foster Griffin. En lo que va de temporada, Griffin lleva un balance de 15-5, con una ERA de 3,67 y un WHIP de 1,19. En general, Griffin ha sido una buena incorporación para el equipo. Ha tenido dos salidas que fueron un poco desastrosas: aguantó cuatro entradas contra los Mets y encajó cinco carreras limpias en su debut con los Guardians.
Los Orioles de Baltimore también le endosaron ocho carreras en 2,1 entradas. En sus otras seis salidas como titular, lanzó 22 entradas y solo encajó 11 carreras. Nunca se ha enfrentado a los Red Sox, así que podría desconcertarlos en la primera vuelta por el orden de bateo.
Los Boston Red Sox son uno de esos equipos que seguramente están rebosantes de confianza. Tras un comienzo de temporada desastroso, dieron un giro y se convirtieron en uno de los equipos más en racha del béisbol justo antes del parón del All-Star. Siguen siendo un equipo con altibajos, pero en la mayoría de sus rachas han ganado partidos en lugar de perderlos. Siguen siendo solo un equipo normalito en Fenway, con un balance de 38-38 en lo que va de temporada. Cuesta casi creerlo, teniendo en cuenta lo bien que lo han hecho, pero llegar al 50 % es impresionante si tenemos en cuenta lo mal que lo hicieron a principios de año.
Los Red Sox van a sacar al único que ha estado imparable en casa todo el año: Sonny Gray. En lo que va de temporada, Sonny Gray lleva un balance de 17-5, con una ERA de 2,82 y un WHIP de 1,16. Debería estar en la pugna por el Premio Cy Young, aunque no va a ganarle a Cam Schlittler. Ha estado muy sólido en septiembre, lanzando 19,1 entradas y cediendo un total de seis carreras limpias. Se enfrentó a los Guardians a principios de temporada y solo cedió una carrera limpia en seis entradas, en una victoria por 9-1 de los Red Sox.
No ha sido solo en ese partido contra los Guardians donde Gray ha destacado. Lleva años jugando genial contra ellos, manteniendo a los bateadores en un promedio de bateo de 0,208 en más de 130 turnos al bate. Aunque los Red Sox no «necesitan» realmente este partido para afianzar su plaza de comodín, igual deberían intentar ganar. Gray ha estado impresionante para ellos y les ha ido muy bien en sus salidas este año. Apuesto por los Red Sox en este partido y también creo que probablemente cubrirán el hándicap de -1,5 carreras. Además, me sorprendería que el total de carreras de este partido fuera inferior a 6,5. Voy a hacer las tres apuestas.
Si quieres más información sobre apuestas deportivas y pronósticos, sigue a David Twitter: @futureprez2024

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Why Potential Reunion with Sonny Gray Makes Sense for Cardinals
item.dc:creator: Curt Bishop; Unknown
item.description: Last offseason, the St. Louis Cardinals traded Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Nolan Arenado and Brendan Donovan, stripping their roster of established veteran players. However, that seemed to have lit a spark underneath the young players they have on their roster. Jordan Walker and JJ Wetherholt have emerged as franchise cornerstones, and though they have cooled off towards the end of the season, there is still a lot to be excited about when concerning the future. item.content:encoded:
Last offseason, the St. Louis Cardinals traded Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Nolan Arenado and Brendan Donovan, stripping their roster of established veteran players. However, that seemed to have lit a spark underneath the young players they have on their roster.
Jordan Walker and JJ Wetherholt have emerged as franchise cornerstones, and though they have cooled off towards the end of the season, there is still a lot to be excited about when concerning the future. The Cardinals also saw Alec Burleson emerge as a star.
Though their starting rotation has been their strength, it could use an addition or two in the offseason. Perhaps a reunion with Sonny Gray could make sense.
Why Sonny Gray reunion would make sense
Gray wasn't quite the ace the Cardinals needed him to be in his two years in St. Louis, but he has been that guy for the Boston Red Sox. In 28 starts, the 36-year-old right-hander is 17-5 with a 2.82 ERA. Though he is older now, he would make sense for the Cardinals because he will likely cost a little less than he did when St. Louis orginally signed him after the 2023 season.
He's also a proven veteran leader that can guide the young pitching staff, and is somebody that can anchor the rotation and get them one step closer to returning to postseason contention, and if they struggle again, he could be a trade candidate at the deadline.
But now might be the right time for the Cardinals to supplement what they have already built from within. They have a strong core in place, and some proven pieces could be what they need to take the next step forward in 2027.
Gray does have a mutual option with Boston for 2027 and has considered retirement, but the mutual option will likely be declined. And if he doesn't retire, perhaps he'll see what the Cardinals have built and be interested in returning to St. Louis.
He is a voice that a lot of the Cardinals' young players are familiar with. He also seemed to enjoy his time in St. Louis despite the team's struggles, and with Kyle Leahy, Quinn Mathews and Michael McGreevy emerging, St. Louis could have an even stronger starting rotation in 2027, especially since the farm system is now loaded with pitching, including top prospect Liam Doyle.
There is a lot to be excited about, and signing Gray could be the first step to getting St. Louis back into contention.
Curt Bishop is a freelance sports writer who graduated from Maryville University of St. Louis with a Bachelor of Arts degree in the field of Communication and currently writes as a contributor for various platforms covering Major League Baseball. Curt’s work includes covering trade and free agency predictions, as well as rumors and news. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox kept outfielder Jarren Duran out of the starting lineup again Wednesday night as they hosted the Cleveland Guardians in the second game of a three-game series at Fenway Park.
Manager Chad Tracy’s posted batting order featured Roman Anthony in left field, Nick Sogard at first base, Jahmai Jones as the designated hitter, Wilyer Abreu in right field, Adley Rutschman behind the plate, Ceddanne Rafaela in center field, Caleb Durbin at third base, Trevor Story at shortstop and Andruw Monasterio at second base. Sonny Gray was listed as the starting pitcher.
Duran also sat Tuesday, when the Guardians beat the Red Sox 3-2. He entered that game as a pinch-hitter and drew a walk.
Cleveland took the series opener on Nathaniel Lowe’s sacrifice fly in the ninth inning. The Guardians stranded 15 runners but still extended their winning streak to six games.
Boston dropped to 84-73. The club already clinched an American League Wild Card berth Sunday but has lost three straight and eight of its last 12.
Duran entered Wednesday batting .204 with 110 hits, 20 home runs, 69 RBIs, 65 runs and 19 stolen bases in 146 games. He had 538 at-bats, 39 walks and 163 strikeouts.
The left-handed hitter has struggled in September. He was 9-for-50 with one home run and one RBI in 17 games this month before Tuesday’s appearance.
Over his last 15 games he was 8-for-42 with one homer. His on-base-plus-slugging percentage sat at .625 for the season.
Rafaela’s return to center field tightened the outfield picture. Anthony has been starting in left and Abreu in right, leaving Duran as the extra outfielder in many recent games.
Tracy had the interim tag removed Tuesday and was named the franchise’s 49th manager. The Red Sox have used a mix of platoons and rest days for Duran down the stretch.
Gray brings a 17-5 record and 2.82 ERA into the start. Cleveland is expected to counter with Forrest Griffin.
The Guardians sit at 82-75 and hold a one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox in the AL Central. Chicago owns the season-series tiebreaker.
Duran, 30, is in his sixth major league season, all with Boston. He was an All-Star in 2024.
He still ranks among the team leaders in home runs and RBIs despite the low batting average. His 20 homers leave him one short of his career high.
The Red Sox close the regular season with this series, then host the Chicago Cubs for three games. Seeding and rest for the Wild Card round remain in play.
Duran’s speed and defense have kept him in the mix even as his batting average dropped. He stole 19 bases and continued to play a plus outfield when used.
Boston’s offense produced eight hits Tuesday. Rutschman went 3-for-4 and pinch-hitter Mickey Gasper tied the game with a home run in the eighth.
Cleveland collected 12 hits. Angel Martínez finished 3-for-4.
The Red Sox sit 12 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East. The Yankees hold the other Wild Card spot six games ahead of Boston.
Duran’s role for the final week and any postseason series will depend on how Tracy balances the four outfielders available.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 18:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: David Butler II)
The Boston Red Sox hope to shift some momentum in advance of the playoffs when they host the Cleveland Guardians on Wednesday night in the second game of a three-game series.
Cleveland extended its winning streak to six games by beating Boston 3-2 on Tuesday. It was the third straight loss for the Red Sox (84-73), who have dropped eight of their last 12 games and own a 9-10 record in September but still clinched a wild-card berth on Sunday.Add left-handed reliever Erik Miller to the list of Boston's concerns as the Red Sox prepare for the playoffs. Miller looked sharp when the Red Sox acquired him from San Francisco in August, but he has allowed nine walks and hit two batters in September.One of those hit batsmen scored the game-winning run Tuesday. Miller hit Chase DeLauter to start the ninth inning, and DeLauter ended up breaking a 2-2 tie when he scored on Nathaniel Lowe's sacrifice fly.Miller has given up six runs and six walks in his past 3 1/3 innings and took the loss on Tuesday.'He's working through stuff,' Boston manager Chad Tracy said. 'I thought today was another step in the right direction. The hit batter ... the free passes are what gets you, and I think he also got some bad batted ball (luck). ... We're gonna try to get him out there a couple more times this week. Obviously still trust the stuff. If we can get that right, trust the stuff and his ability to strike out guys.'
Tuesday's win allowed the Guardians (82-75) to remain one game ahead of the Chicago White Sox at the top of the American League Central standings. Chicago has the division tiebreaker over Cleveland, which has a magic number of two to clinch a playoff berth.
Meanwhile, Guardians manager Stephen Vogt called Lowe 'a professional hitter.'
'You know he's not trying to do too much,' Vogt said. 'He's not going up there trying to be a hero, hitting a three-run homer. Just score the guy from third. Got a pitch up in the zone, and was able to drive it deep enough to left. And you know he continues to just make plays for us.'The Guardians won despite stranding 15 runners and a 1-for-12 hitting performance with runners in scoring position.'Again, felt like it was another night where we get a ton of traffic, we put a lot of pressure on, and just weren't able to get the big hit,' Vogt said. 'You know, we were able to get a couple runs across, but we left a lot on the table. But I just love the way we're making guys work. We're getting on base ... and we're going to come through a lot more often than not. And again, our pitching just picked us up again tonight.'Tracy said he expects center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela (quadriceps) to be activated from the injured list on Wednesday. The manager also said first baseman Willson Contreras still has some soreness in his hand and won't be in the lineup Wednesday but is close to returning.Right-hander Sonny Gray (17-5, 2.82 ERA) will start for the Red Sox on Wednesday. He's 8-5 with a 3.12 ERA in 21 career starts against the Guardians. On May 30, he gave up one run on four hits and three walks over six innings against them. He struck out seven in a 9-1 win.Left-hander Foster Griffin (15-5, 3.67 ERA) will start for Cleveland on Wednesday. It will be his first career appearance against the Red Sox.--Field Level Media

item.title: [dailycampus.com] Brayden’s Breakdown: Boston Red Sox postseason preview
item.dc:creator: Brayden Gorski
item.description: The Boston Red Sox clinched their second consecutive playoff berth Sunday and their third since 2021. It was a season with the highest of highs and the lowest of lows in Boston as they started the season 10-17 before firing longtime manager Alex Cora. In June, the Red Sox found themselves 14 games under .500 at a record of 32-46. This is when everything changed. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox clinched their second consecutive playoff berth Sunday and their third since 2021.
It was a season with the highest of highs and the lowest of lows in Boston as they started the season 10-17 before firing longtime manager Alex Cora.
In June, the Red Sox found themselves 14 games under .500 at a record of 32-46. This is when everything changed.
They swept the New York Yankees before losing two out of three games to the Washington Nationals.
The Red Sox went on the road and swept the Los Angeles Angels, Chicago White Sox and New York Mets to sit at 46-48 heading into the all-star break.
After nine straight road wins, the Red Sox headed home to face the 56-38 Tampa Bay Rays. Tampa has had Boston’s number in the past few seasons, but this weekend was different.
In the first game of a doubleheader after the break, the Red Sox took care of business 10-0. Then in the night cap, Tampa Bay Rays took an early 2-0 before outfielder Wilyer Abreu decided the next 24 hours were all about him. He hit two home runs on the way to a 5-3 Red Sox win.
The next game was the defining game of the winning streak. The Rays were matching the Sox in scoring all-game before Abreu stepped to the plate down 6-5 in the seventh. Abreu crushed a two-run homer to right field, sending himself and Fenway Park into a frenzy. His fourth home run in 24 hours put Boston up 7-6, a lead they would hold for 12 consecutive wins.
They swept Tampa the next day before taking the first two games of the series versus the Orioles to tie a franchise record 15 straight wins. That first win did not come without drama. A back-and-forth game was knotted up in the eighth when Caleb Durbin smacked a game winning homerun to left field. The “Durbinator” had a rough start to the season but became one of the centerpieces of this win streak.
The streak would end at 15 but just a week later, Boston would rip off another nine straight wins. Durbin hit a walk-off single in an instant classic 12-11 victory against the White Sox. Ceddanne Rafaela became the king of LA for a few days after smacking four home runs in three games against the back-to-back champs.
So here we are, the Red Sox are 84-72 with a firm grip on the second wild card spot in the American League. Now, the New York Yankees stand in their way.
The Yankees beat the Red Sox 2-1 in the three-game wildcard series last year, and Boston is looking for revenge this season.
The pitching will be the key for both teams. Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray and Ranger Suarez will toe the rubber for Boston against the Yankees’ Gerritt Cole, Max Fried and Massachusetts’ own Cam Schlittler in the series.
In his first full season in the MLB, Tolle hit his stride. The southpaw posted a 3.02 ERA and a 10.4 K/9. He is also peaking at the right time, sporting a 0.75 ERA in two starts during September.
In a complete 180 from Tolle, Gray has been dominant in what may be his swan song in the majors. After being acquired via trade in the offseason, Gray has won 17 games, a career high for the veteran. He pitched 7.1 innings of one hit baseball while striking out nine in a June win over the Yankees.
Suarez signed a 5-year $130 million dollar contract with Boston in the offseason and has been solid as a member of the Sox. However, the 2026 all-star struggled in all three of his starts against the Yankees. The Bronx Bombers were 3-0 against Suarez.
Despite great performances by the Yankees, Suarez is a playoff pitcher. He had a 1.48 ERA in 42.2 postseason innings as a member of the Philadelphia Phillies. In Philadelphia’s 2022 run to the World Series, the Phillies won all five games Suarez pitched in. He only allowed two earned runs in 14.2 innings pitched in 2022.
Along with the starters, the back of the bullpen has been nails for Boston. Erik Miller, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman handled the seventh, eighth and ninth innings for interim manager Chad Tracy and the Red Sox. Miller came over at the trade deadline and did not allow an earned run in his first 10 appearances. Whitlock has been a staple in the Red Sox bullpen since 2021 and is possibly having his best year yet. He has a 1.75 ERA in 53 appearances. Chapman continues to age like fine wine. The 38-year-old was named an all-star for the second straight year and is 34/36 in save situations this year.
The rest of the hitters for the Red Sox will need to do some heavy lifting if they want to compete with the Yankees. Boston acquired Adley Rutschman at the deadline, and the catcher will be required to switch hit and catch in the playoffs. Wilson Contreras and Trevor Story will add postseason experience to the lineup while former top prospect Roman Anthony and local legend Mickey Gasper will look to provide during their first playoff at bats.
If the standings hold, the Red Sox and Yankees will battle in the Bronx on Tuesday for the wildcard series, a statement no Red Sox fan would have believed in June.

item.title: [Away Back Gone] Guardians' late rally poked another hole in Red Sox's suddenly shaky playoff bullpen plan

item.description: The final week of the MLB season always features plenty of altered and adjusted pitching plans. item.content:encoded:
The final week of the MLB season always features plenty of altered and adjusted pitching plans.
Normally the one consistent throughout the drumbeat of the 162-game MLB season is a team’s pitching plan; regardless of whether a team has an ace on the mound or is going with pitching madness, the goal is always to get the best position to win while taking it a day at a time.
But that's a bit different this week.
While some teams are playing out the string and giving their starters one last opportunity to pitch before drifting off into the winter, the teams that have already clinched are stuck in the limbo of trying to cover the now while also preparing for the postseason.
It’s not like football or basketball where you can just throw random backups out there. Every inning needs to be covered, and there’s only so many innings you can give to pitchers who aren’t a part of your postseason plans.
Even if the Guardians won’t be in that position for a couple days (even if they clinch a postseason spot later today the American League Central race still won’t be settled, the Boston Red Sox's already know their postseason fate by virtue of being all but locked into the American League’s No. 5 seed.
We got an early example of how that could change their pitching plans on Monday when manager Andy Tracy pulled budding ace Peyton Tolle after five innings, and we got another example of it later in the game whenTracy went to Erik Miller in the ninth inning of a tied game instead of going to Aroldis Chapman… and Miller gave up the go-ahead run on a Nathaniel Lowe sacrifice fly.
The Red Sox are already playing with their postseason plans in mind, and those plans just got a bit more convoluted thanks to Miller’s rough outing.
The Red sox's bullpen struggles could help the Guardians in their quest to make the postseason
While Miller has largely been excellent since the Red Sox acquired him in August, he’s now allowed a run in three straight appearances and seems to be falling down manager Andy Tracy’s trust tree.
Miller opened his outing by hitting Chase DeLauter on the forearm with a pitch before surrendering a single to Jo Adell that was followed by Lowe’s sacrifice fly.
After the game, Tracy said that Miller was “working through some things,” which was obvious to everyone in the ballpark and watching at home.
Those struggles set up what should be an interesting last two games at Fenway Park. The Sox have two of their best pitchers going in the final two games of the series (Sonny Gray today and Ranger Suarez tomorrow), and it’s hard to believe the Red Sox are going to give them a ton of run in either of their starts.
While the Guardians may not get a chance to benefit from Boston’s relief struggles in the postseason since Boston will likely be locked into the other side of the bracket, they can use it to their benefit over the next 48 hours as they work to nail down a postseason spot.

item.content:encoded:
Garrett Crochet ruined Game 1 for the AL Wild Card series last year for the Yankees.
And he could be looking to inflict damage on Boston’s AL East rivals once again.
The sidelined lefty ace said he hit 96 mph in a live batting practice session Tuesday and believes he can contribute in the postseason.
“The way that … just went, I could go get outs,” Crochet said, according to the Boston Globe. “It depends obviously what role they want me in. It’s not really for me to say. I know myself and I know my body, and the biggest thing was that I felt good out there. Felt like I was able to ramp up intensity to a place that I haven’t gone yet. Tomorrow is going to be a big deal, seeing how I recover.”
The Yankees and Red Sox are seemingly on a collision course for a second straight Wild Card clash, although Boston has yet to secure the No. 5 seed.
The loser of the AL Central battle between the Guardians and White Sox can still overtake Boston for that date in The Bronx next Tuesday.
Boston entered last postseason with Crochet anchoring its rotation off a season that earned him second place in the AL Cy Young voting but question marks in the rotation after him.
This time around, Boston has established starters but Crochet is the question mark.
Crochet is closing in on five months since he last pitched in an MLB game after landing on the injured list in April with left shoulder inflammation, having last started April 25.
He did not pitch up to his standards in his six outings before being sidelined, posting a 6.30 ERA while allowing 33 hits and five homers in just 30 innings.
It’s uncertain how Boston would use him in the postseason due to the long layoff and the team having quality starters.
Lefties Peyton Tolle, Ranger Suarez and Jake Bennett plus righty Sonny Gray give Boston four capable starters to match up with the Yankees.
Last season, Crochet dominated the Yankees in Game 1, striking out 11 while allowing just one run in 7 2/3 innings in Boston’s 3-1 victory.
Brayan Bello lasted just 2 1/3 innings in a Game 2 loss and rookie Connelly Early logged only 3 2/3 innings in the decisive Game 3 loss.
“He’s definitely making progress,” Boston manager Chad Tracy — fresh off his promotion to full-time skipper — said, per the Boston Globe. “Again, it’s ‘see how he feels tomorrow.’ I know that there’s a lot of conversation around that because we’re only a week away from the postseason now. So determining how does he feel coming out of that [and] what does this weekend look like is going to be the next step.
“What that looks like now, I don’t know. I just know that whatever it is, it’s going to be done with Garrett’s best interest in mind, making sure that we’re doing it right.”
Crochet noted that he would “feel bad” taking someone’s spot on the roster, and said he would accept whatever the front office decides.
With the season ending Sunday, Boston does not have any soft landing spots to allow Crochet to face major-league hitters in a true game environment before the playoffs begin.
Boston ultimately may just have to trust that its star pitcher can return with no hiccups.
“You’re considering all those things,” Tracy said, per the Boston Globe. “We have to consider it and just be very, very mindful of, again, what are we potentially exposing him to and what can he give us really?”

item.content:encoded:
BOSTON — Nathaniel Lowe had a tiebreaking sacrifice fly off reliever Erik Miller in the ninth inning, and the Cleveland Guardians maintained their slim in the AL Central with a 3-2 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Tuesday night.
Angel Martínez had three hits for the Guardians, who entered the day with a one-game lead over the White Sox atop the division. Chicago owns the tiebreaker by winning the season series. Cleveland stranded 15 baserunners.
The loss was Boston’s eighth in 12 games, spoiling Chad Tracy’s first game as manager after the club named him its 49th in team history.
Adley Rutschman added three hits for Boston, which clinched one of the AL’s wild-card spots on Sunday.
Boston pinch hitter Mickey Gasper hit Hunter Gaddis’ first pitch, tying it at 2-2 leading off the eighth.
Gaddis (5-3) got the win and Cade Smith recorded the final three outs for his 40th save.
Miller (4-2) hit a batter and gave up two hits in an inning.
A strong candidate for the AL Rookie of the Year, Cleveland left-hander Parker Messick gave up a run over five innings. He lowered his ERA to 2.55 and is on pace to become the fourth rookie starting pitcher in MLB history with an ERA under 2.60 and averaging 9.0 or more strikeouts per nine innings.
In his tune-up for a likely playoff start next week, Boston lefty Payton Tolle struggled with his control over 5 2/3 innings, giving up two runs on eight hits.
Up next
Guardians LHP Foster Griffin (15-5, 3.67 ERA) is set to face Red Sox RHP Sonny Gray (17-5, 2.82) on Wednesday in the middle game of the three-game series.

item.content:encoded:
After an off day on Monday, the Boston Red Sox will return to Fenway Park to begin the next-to-last series of the regular season before the playoffs next week. Boston clinched their spot in the postseason after the Atlanta Braves completed a three-game sweep of the Houston Astros on Sunday afternoon.
The Red Sox are all but locked into the second American League wild-card spot. They are on a collision course with the New York Yankees next week in the Bronx for a best-of-three series. Before then, however, Boston has three games with the Cleveland Guardians. They will then host the Chicago Cubs this weekend, weather permitting.
As for the Guardians series, Wilyer Abreu is back in the lineup for manager Chad Tracy and batting in a familiar spot.
Boston Red Sox Announce Wilyer Abreu Spot in Lineup Against Guardians on Tuesday Night
Tracy will send left-hander Payton Tolle to the mound to open the series and as far as his lineup goes, Abreu us back and batting cleanup. Here is Boston's lineup for the series opener against Cleveland's Parker Messick,
Nick Sogard 1B
Jahmai Jones DH
Wilyer Abreu RF
Caleb Durbin 3B
Isiah Kiner-Falefa SS
Nate Eaton CF
Abreu will be batting fourth, with first baseman Willson Contreras still out of the lineup after getting hit by a pitch last Thursday night against the Texas Rangers. He missed the series against the Tampa Bay Rays. As for Abreu, he did not play in Sunday's series finale, a 5-1 loss.
Boston Red Sox Playing Out the String Ahead of Playoffs
Tuesday, it was announced that Tracy was having the interim tag removed, and Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow is having his option in 2029 and 2030 picked up by the club. It's not surprising that it was announced before the playoffs.
Boston is scheduled to send their three projected starters on the mound next week against the Yankees: Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suárez against the Guardians. However, Cleveland is in a heated race with the Chicago White Sox for the American League Central Division title. They enter the series with a one-game lead over the White Sox, who are playing the Kansas City Royals this week.
Boston has slumped in September. However, they can use the six games before next week as a tune-up. As for this weekend, the weather is projected to be a mess. Tim Healy of the Boston Globe reported that MLB has no plans to move the series out of Boston. There are going to be very few windows to play baseball this weekend.
The Cubs are in a battle for home-field advantage in the National League wild-card round. Those games will have big meaning for them and the NL. They enter play this week tied with the San Diego Padres for home-field advantage next week. The Philadelphia Phillies are a game behind. There is a lot riding on this weekend.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Boston Red Sox Announce Wilyer Abreu Decision Before Cleveland Guardians Series appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [bosoxinjection.com] Red Sox might've cemented Craig Breslow’s rise off the hot seat too soon
item.dc:creator: Brian Burrows
item.description: The Craig Breslow era in Boston has felt like a roller coaster ride. Hired at the start of the 2023-24 offseason, the Boston Red Sox have not had a losing season under Breslow, despite wild swings in the team's form over the three years. With the Red Sox clinching a playoff berth for the second year in a row, team ownership decided that now was the time to exercise two options on their Chief Baseball Officer's contract, guaranteeing his deal for the 2029 and 2030 seasons. item.content:encoded:
The Craig Breslow era in Boston has felt like a roller coaster ride. Hired at the start of the 2023-24 offseason, the Boston Red Sox have not had a losing season under Breslow, despite wild swings in the team's form over the three years.
With the Red Sox clinching a playoff berth for the second year in a row, team ownership decided that now was the time to exercise two options on their Chief Baseball Officer's contract, guaranteeing his deal for the 2029 and 2030 seasons. On the surface, a head of baseball operations who got his team to the playoffs in years two and three of their time running the club getting years added to their contract, would make sense, but in Breslow's case it isn't as straightforward.
It was only three months ago when most of Red Sox Nation was calling for Breslow's head. The Red Sox were 32-46 on June 24, dead last in the division, and it already seemed like the season was over. It took a miraculous turnaround to get the team to the playoffs. Not to say that Breslow had nothing to do with that; he had added a lot of players to the roster who were key contributors, but that has a lot more to do with the players and coaches than the front office.
Breslow's tenure has also been marred by controversy, specifically the Rafael Devers drama. It was his handling of the situation, along with former manager Alex Cora, that ultimately led to the fracture of the relationship with the team's then-face of the franchise. While the fanbase was split on whose side they took, player or team, his actions after the fact didn't make it any better.
Red Sox's Craig Breslow had the hottest seat of any GM only three months ago
It was the signing of Alex Bregman that caused the Devers drama in the first place. While Breslow was praised for the signing, Bregman opted out at the end of the year and was then not re-signed. The Red Sox went from two elite third basemen to none in the span of a season. It wasn't a good look for the Red Sox CBO.
Now, Breslow's pivot from all of the drama and mess surrounding Devers and Bregman looks incredibly good in hindsight. The additions of Ranger Suarez, Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Caleb Durbin, and others have been extremely impactful to the Red Sox's success this season. While some of those moves were celebrated at the time they happened, others like the Durbin-Kyle Harrison swap (that also netted the Red Sox Andruw Monasterio and Anthony Seigler) were heavily scrutinized.
Breslow also made good moves at the trade deadline, adding Erik Miller and Eli White, who have looked good for the Sox. He also made the splash trade for Adley Rutschman, which hasn't worked as well on the field, but certainly instilled confidence in the team, knowing the front office believed in them.
Red Sox could've softened the impact by extending one of Craig Breslow's options at first
All of this is to say that Breslow's time as CBO hasn't been as smooth sailing as the records would suggest. He has had some high highs but also some low lows. Why did ownership feel the need to exercise both options right now? The first option wasn't needed until the 2029 season, two years out. The second was for 2030, three years out.
Doing the first one now would've been fine — picking up the 2029 option gives Breslow another three comfortable seasons on his contract. That would make him more comfortable making moves for the future and give him the job security to know he will likely be in place to see them play out. Selecting the 2030 option on the same day was unnecessary, though.
There have been too many hiccups in the three years under Breslow to say he has warranted another four seasons. The start of 2026 could easily repeat itself in 2027. Should ownership feel the need to relieve him of his duties early, then this makes it that much harder. Breslow hasn't won a World Series in Boston; in fact, he hasn't even made it out of the Wild Card round. Exercising the option for 2030 feels very premature.
Breslow has not done a bad job in Boston. At the end of the day, it's results that matter, and Breslow's teams have made the playoffs two out of three times. He shouldn't be fearing for his job, but his contract also wasn't ending for another two seasons. It feels early to be handing him the keys so far down the road after the drama of his first two years as CBO.

item.title: [bosoxinjection.com] Red Sox’s rotation against Guardians could preview Wild Card Game 1 starter fans desperately want
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: The postseason begins on September 29, giving teams one day of rest between the end of the regular season and the start of the race. Playoff teams must plan their rotations early have the right pitchers rested and ready for the opening series and the Boston Red Sox have seemingly made their call. The Red Sox's rotation for their upcoming matchup with the Cleveland Guardians, their second-to-last series of the year, is Payton Tolle in game one, Sonny Gray in game two and Ranger Suarez in game thr
item.content:encoded:
The postseason begins on September 29, giving teams one day of rest between the end of the regular season and the start of the race. Playoff teams must plan their rotations early have the right pitchers rested and ready for the opening series and the Boston Red Sox have seemingly made their call.
The Red Sox's rotation for their upcoming matchup with the Cleveland Guardians, their second-to-last series of the year, is Payton Tolle in game one, Sonny Gray in game two and Ranger Suarez in game three. That leaves Patrick Sandoval, Jake Bennett and Brayan Bello (or a bullpen game) for the final series against the Chicago Cubs, not necessarily in that order.
Tolle has earned the series-opening start against the New York Yankees. He's posted a 2.36 ERA and 0.88 WHIP with 56 strikeouts over his last seven starts. He's stayed hot despite having 143 innings on his arm this year, and he's gotten even better as the year has gone on.
Tolle has had previous success against the Yankees, including two stellar outings this year. He faced the Yankees in his first big league appearance this year and allowed just one run on three hits with 11 strikeouts and a walk over six innings. Tolle next faced New York on June 26 (one of the games in the four-game sweep that started Boston's historic summer winning streak) and he pitched seven, one-hit innings with seven strikeouts.
Red Sox-Guardians series likely previews Boston's Wild Card rotation with Payton Tolle starting Game 1
Starting Tolle first could set up a battle between two young lefties and Cy Young Award contenders (though it isn't much of a contest) if the Yankees plan to open the series with their ace Cam Schlittler. This might not be the case, though, as New York seems to be setting Gerrit Cole up for the Game 1 start. The Red Sox don't fare as well against right-handed pitching as they do against lefties, with a .712 team OPS against them, and taking Boston off its game will be a high priority for its rival.
Whether the Red Sox win or lose Game 1, Game 2 means everything. With a series loss or a sweep on the line, Boston's ace Gray should take the mound. The 36-year-old Gray has surprised fans everywhere by posting one of the best seasons of his career with the Red Sox and his consistency is unmatched.
Gray has clocked a 2.82 ERA, 1.16 WHIP, 146 strikeouts and 45 walks over 163 innings. Like the Red Sox, the Yankees also don't perform especially well against righty pitching, with a .713 OPS as a club. With a sweep on the line or to stay alive, the veteran Gray is the guy to trust.
In a win-or-go-home Game 3, Suarez deserves Boston's trust. He's gotten back on his feet over the last few weeks following a shaky spell (5.70 ERA in August) after a groin injury. Postseason starts are Suarez's bread and butter — he boasts a 1.48 ERA and 1.06 WHIP over 42.2 frames across seven playoff series — and he's the best choice to keep the Red Sox alive when they're on the brink of elimination.
Boston's rotation has been the biggest strength of the team all season. With these three pitchers, in any order, the Red Sox have good chances to get past the Yankees to advance to the Division Series. But setting the energy with Tolle and having the two veterans follow, as Boston has set things up, makes a lot of sense.

Regardless of how the Sox choose to stack the deck, this will be Tolle’s final tune up before
item.content:encoded:
Chad Tracy told us not to look very much into the order of the rotation this week, but it’s hard not to note that Payton Tolle is starting tonight exactly one week before the Wild Card series begins, and Sonny Gray and Ranger Suarez are set to go tomorrow and Thursday. That feels like a Game 1, Game 2, and Game 3 setup for New York, but again, we’ll still have to wait a few more days for official word.
Regardless of how the Sox choose to stack the deck, this will be Tolle’s final tune up before the showdown against the Yankees, so how he looks here will be even more important than the result of this game for the Red Sox.
On the contrary, this game means everything to Cleveland. Despite entering the night three games behind the Red Sox, they’re currently leading the AL Central by a game over the Chicago White Sox, and if the season ended today, they’d actually get a bye and wouldn’t even have to play in the Wild Card round.
To help them maintain control of that bye, they have their ace Parker Messick on the mound, who enters the evening with a 2.57 ERA and 186 strike outs on the season.
Switching gears to the Red Sox lineup, the biggest note is that Roman Anthony is again in left field and Jarren Duran starts the night on the bench. This is becoming the theme against left handed starts, which is obviously noteworthy for next week because Carlos Rodon and Max Fried are both left handed.

item.content:encoded:
With just a few games remaining in the regular season, the chances of a Red Sox vs. Yankees matchup in the AL Wild Card round appear high.
If the Rays can officially clinch the AL East, and the Red Sox can pull away from the White Sox for the AL's No. 5 seed, Boston will be traveling to face New York in a best-of-three matchup.
So when Aaron Boone announced the latest on Aaron Judge's injury status on Tuesday, it carried massive implications for the Red Sox as they begin looking toward the postseason.
Here's the latest on Judge and what it could mean for the Red Sox.
How Yankees' Aaron Judge Injury Update Affects Red Sox
On Tuesday, Boone told reporters that Judge, who was recently played on the 10-day IL with a calf strain just days after his return from a significant injury, is dealing with a "moderate grade" strain.
However, more significantly, Boone said the Yankees aren't preparing for Judge to be ready for the start of the postseason after he had a PPP injection on Monday.
"We’re planning on him not being a part of that,” Boone said, per Bryan Hoch.
While Judge's status for a likely wild-card matchup won't become official until early next week, when the Yankees would have to finalize their roster for a series, it's looking unlikely that he will be healthy in time.
For the Red Sox, no Judge would change the dynamic of attacking the Yankees' lineup. While Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger remain power threats themselves, the presence of the three-time AL MVP boosts New York's offense to an elite status. Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez and Payton Tolle — likely to pitch for Boston in a best-of-three series — wouldn't have to worry about the threat of Judge's bat breaking a game open in one swing.
Red Sox vs. Yankees is not yet official, and neither is Judge's status for the postseason. But as of Tuesday, all indications are that New York will have to host Boston without its superstar outfielder.

item.title: [bosoxinjection.com] Red Sox just buried a Craig Breslow show of faith in Chad Tracy news drop
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: After a rollercoaster of a season which included a brutal start, sudden managerial firings, historic win streaks and a playoff clinch, the Boston Red Sox have extended the man who brought it all together. Boston has removed Chad Tracy's "interim" tag and made him their manager, first reported by Christopher Smith of MassLive. item.content:encoded:
After a rollercoaster of a season which included a brutal start, sudden managerial firings, historic win streaks and a playoff clinch, the Boston Red Sox have extended the man who brought it all together. Boston has removed Chad Tracy's "interim" tag and made him their manager, first reported by Christopher Smith of MassLive.
Tracy and the Red Sox have agreed to a three-year contract with a club option in 2030, per Smith. His salary has not yet been reported.
Tracy was Boston's Triple-A manager on April 25, the day Alex Cora and six other members of his coaching staff were fired. The Red Sox then flew him out to Baltimore to take over in a whirlwind and a leap of faith, and it worked. He'll be the 49th manager in Red Sox franchise history (subscription required).
The Red Sox had a 10-17 record on the day of Tracy's promotion and he managed the club to two games below .500 by July 12, the start of the All-Star break. Boston's historic 15-game winning streak had already begun by then — it rallied to sweep the New York Yankees in four games two weeks before, lost a series to the Washington Nationals, and it was all winning from there.
Red Sox name Chad Tracy manager through 2029, exercised club options to keep Craig Breslow CBO through 2030
Tracy had long been revered as the manager of the WooSox and it didn't take long for Red Sox fans to become equally endeared to him. His direct, but friendly communication style offered a stark contrast to other leaders in the organization. He had preexisting relationships with many of the organization's young players from their time in Triple-A and from rehab assignments, and it showed. After the Red Sox's historic July and August spell, Tracy's promotion seemed almost inevitable, and rightfully so.
Within the Tracy contract announcement, the Red Sox also included another contract update. The Red Sox have exercised the 2029-30 club options on Craig Breslow's contract, essentially extending him for another two years.
This is quite a sign of trust from Boston. Breslow's tenure started with some massive moves like the Garrett Crochet trade, and the Red Sox made the playoffs for the first time in three seasons with him at the helm. But his communication style has been criticized, it's led to massive trades of players who were supposed to be fixtiures of the organization for years to come, and front office leaks have marred his public image.
But Breslow has loosened up a bit since the beginning of the season. He's been pictured around the players more often and has been cracking jokes on his radio appearances.
There's also no denying that he had a great 2025-26 offseason. Sonny Gray, Willson Contreras, Ranger Suarez and Caleb Durbin, all acquired by Breslow over the offseason, are all major parts of the Red Sox's success.
Cora had been Boston's manager for eight seasons and many Red Sox fans couldn't stand Breslow at the beginning of June. Things can change quickly in baseball.
